newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-TEMPERAMENTAL KEEPER FINALLY TAKES STEP TOO FAR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TEMPERAMENTAL KEEPER FINALLY TAKES STEP TOO FAR.

text.p: For little Pascal Olmeta growing up in a tough Corsican town, the line between right and wrong was hard to discern.
"In the quarter where I grew up, Lupino, some have died, some are in prison and others have become ministers," Olmeta said.
"Where I come from the line between cop and crook is not clear. For me, everything hung in the balance the day my dad found a wallet.
"We were a family of five kids, poor, and he hesitated. Finally he handed it in. It was borderline.
"In short, all this to say I could have turned bad."

The lesson had an impact and the young Olmeta began a soccer career with Bastia and went on to become one of France's best goalkeepers, though his fiery Mediterranean temperament won him a reputation as being both outspoken and controversial.
But Olmeta, now 35, crossed the thin line to the wrong side for a second time last month and has now lost his job with first division club Lyon.

Last Wednesday, Lyon announced they had sacked Olmeta after he punched team mate Jean-Luc Sassus twice in the changing rooms after their 1-0 home league defeat by Nantes on December 20. It was thought to be a reaction to Lyon conceding a late goal.
Olmeta has said through his lawyer that he plans to contest Lyon's decision, but so far he has not made any public comment on the incident.

Lyon, whom Olmeta joined from Marseille in 1993, said they would not stand in his way of finding a new club, but with the mid-season transfer deadline past, he can play abroad for the rest of this season only.
Midfielder Sylvain Deplace said: "On a sporting level, it's a big loss. On the big occasions in particular, he had the art of super-motivating us."
Little more than a year ago, Olmeta was immersed in scandal when he was put under investigation over alleged use of false 200 franc ($40) bank notes. He was later cleared.
His tough guy image was enhanced by a boxing challenge against big rugby forward Daniel Moscato some years ago.
He says he has since sought advice in books and from specialists on how to stop reacting to trouble by fighting.

Olmeta, who played for Marseille in the 1991 European Cup final, claimed in 1985 when he was 24 that he was the best goalkeeper in the country and ought to play for France. The closest he got to a full cap was winning selection in the squad.
